_info.comment: The half of the SSTORE branch table that needs a slot which was ALREADY NON-ZERO when the transaction began. Every other state fixture in this suite declares empty pre-storage, so `original == 0` in all of them and four of the rule's branches were unreachable by construction -- not four oversights but one structural property of how the corpus was authored. Five slots, each pre-set to 9, each bracketed by its own gas reading.
_info.eip: EIP-2200 at Phoenix, EIP-2929 at Magneto, EIP-3529 at Mystique. All three reuse one branch table; only the constants and the cold/warm layer differ.
_info.branches: Named by the production client's own numbering in gasSStoreEIP2200 / makeGasSStoreFunc. Slot 1: 2.1.2, write existing slot. Slot 2: 2.1.2b then 2.2.1.1, delete then recreate -- the refund is added and then SUBTRACTED again. Slot 3: 2.1.2 then 2.2.1.2, change then delete while dirty. Slot 4: 2.1.2 then 2.2.2.2, change then reset to the original non-zero value. Slot 5: branch 1, a no-op write of the same value, which is a no-op ONLY from Phoenix -- before it, writing 9 over 9 still pays the reset price.
_info.slots: 1 to 5 hold the written values. 0x11 to 0x15 hold the gas each sequence consumed. 0x1f is the liveness marker.
_info.whyThisMattersForEIP3529: EIP-3529's entire content is reducing the clearing refund from 15000 to 4800. That constant is consumed at THREE sites -- 2.1.2b, 2.2.1.1 and 2.2.1.2 -- and before this fixture only 2.1.2b was asserted, by sstore_clear_refund.json. A build that reduced the refund at that one site and left the other two at 15000 passed the whole suite. Slots 2 and 3 reach the other two.
_info.stillNotAsserted: The EIP-2200 reentrancy sentry -- SSTORE fails outright when 2300 or less gas remains -- is the reason EIP-2200 exists rather than EIP-1283, and no fixture here reaches it. It needs a call with bounded gas rather than a storage sequence, so it is separate work, named so it is not mistaken for covered.
_info.oracle: core-geth's own statetest runner, which is not the implementation under certification. Each expectation is the state root that runner computes for this body at that fork's rules, chain id 61.
_info.oracle-version: core-geth modernized 1.13.0-26975d6a. Production v1.12.21 cannot be used: its t8n fork table has no ETC_DieHard, ETC_Gotham or ETC_DefuseDifficultyBomb.
_info.verification: 2026-08-25: 12/12 subtests pass under evm statetest. Scored against deliberately wrong builds; see wrongBuildScores.
_info.boundaries: Three, and they land where the rules say. Frontier through Agharta share one root -- legacy metering, which this chain kept while Ethereum briefly ran EIP-1283. Phoenix moves it (EIP-2200). Magneto moves it again (EIP-2929 cold access). Mystique moves it a third time (EIP-3529). Spiral does not move it, which is an assertion.
_info.signing: txbytes carries the signed transaction. Legacy signature through Gas Reprice, replay-protected from Die Hard, matching this chain's own adoption of EIP-155.
_info.unfilled-no-fork-name: No expectation for ETC_Thanos: the generator's fork table has no name for it. A tooling gap, not a claim that the case does not apply.
_info.unfilled-not-a-state-rule: No expectation for ETC_DAOFork, ETC_DAOWars, ETC_FrontierThawing, ETC_MESSOff, ETC_MESSOn: these change no state-transition rule.

wrongBuildScores.method: A real client was patched and rebuilt, not reasoned about. EIP-3529's reduced clearing refund was applied at the clean-delete site (2.1.2b) and left at the old 15000 at the two dirty sites (2.2.1.1, 2.2.1.2) -- the precise defect this fixture was written to catch, and a plausible one, since a reader fixing 'the' refund constant naturally finds the first of three.
wrongBuildScores.result: This fixture catches it. THIRTY-FIVE of the suite's other state fixtures pass that build silently, including sstore_clear_refund.json, which asserts the one site the patch left correct.
wrongBuildScores.howItFails: Not as a root mismatch. The client PANICS: `Refund counter below zero (gas: 15000 > refund: 4800)` at operations_acl.go:74. Slot 2 deletes a slot (adding the correct 4800) and then recreates it (subtracting the wrong 15000), driving the refund counter negative. A client shipping this defect crashes on any transaction that does the same, which makes it consensus-critical rather than merely a mispriced operation.
wrongBuildScores.whatThisDemonstrates: Coverage is not discrimination. Before this fixture, every ledger in the repository recorded EIP-3529 as covered, and it was -- at one of the three sites its only constant is consumed. The other two were free to be arbitrarily wrong.
